unextracted: a macro; the extractor records declarations, not macros
why:
phase-417 stage 3 (2026-09-11) -- CLOSED, together with issue 1019, which is the same family losing a different field.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `RCLCPP_FATAL(logger, ...)` emits at the FATAL severity, on the logger it is handed.

OURS WAS: `do { (void)(logger); NROS_ERROR(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/logging.hpp`). One line, three defects, and the whole `RCLCPP_*` family shared them:
  1. `NROS_ERROR` is the legacy printf family, whose sink is `fprintf(stderr)` on a hosted build and a NO-OP on a freestanding one. On Zephyr, FreeRTOS, NuttX and ThreadX -- the targets nano-ros exists for -- a ported node's entire log output was compiled away with no diagnostic. It worked on the host, which is where anyone would test the port. This is issue 1019's first defect.
  2. the logger was cast to `void`, so per-logger levels applied to none of the family and `rclcpp::get_logger("planner")` selected nothing. Issue 1019's third defect.
  3. FATAL lowered to ERROR, because the legacy family has no fatal level at all. This row.

FIX, one change for all three: the family routes at `NROS_LOG_*` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/rclc/log.h`), which dispatches through `nros_log` -- so it reaches `LOG_ERR`/`printk` on exactly the targets where the legacy sink is a no-op, honours the per-logger threshold, and has a distinct `RCLC_LOG_SEVERITY_FATAL`. `rclcpp::get_logger(name)` now RESOLVES the name through `rclc_log_get_logger` (phase-417 W4.d landed the C surface that made this possible) instead of building a null-handled sentinel. `NROS_INFO` and friends are UNCHANGED and still correct for a board's own console print; what was wrong was routing `RCLCPP_*` through them.

THE FALLBACK IS LOAD-BEARING: `rclc_log_emit_fmt_at` RETURNS EARLY on a null handle, so re-pointing the family at it without more would have swapped one silent drop for another -- a `Logger` built from a name alone, or from an uninitialised node, carries a null handle. `rclcpp::detail::log_handle` sends those to the catch-all `nros` logger, which is where a record with no owner belongs, and the probe asserts it.

ONE CONSEQUENCE, named: `RCLCPP_DEBUG` no longer compiles out under `NDEBUG`. It is runtime-filtered by the logger's threshold now, which is what upstream does.

ENFORCEMENT BOUND, restated because it has not changed: neither `api-parity.py` extractor emits C/C++ MACROS (the recorded rclcpp surface has 226 records and no macro among them), so `--check` will never reach this row. A TEST is the only thing that can hold it, and there is one: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_loudness_runtime.cpp` links `libnros_cpp.a`, installs a real sink through `rclc_log_add_sink`, and asserts that each `RCLCPP_*` record ARRIVES, at the RIGHT SEVERITY, carrying its MESSAGE and its LOGGER NAME -- a sink is the only observer that can tell "the record reached nros_log at FATAL" from "something printed to stderr", which is precisely the distinction issue 1019 is about. Negative control against the pre-fix headers: 12 failures and ZERO records captured, with the console showing `[ERROR] ... fatal-marker 4` -- this row's defect, printed.

The refusal macros this header now also defines are `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_SPIN`, `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_SPIN_RUNTIME` and `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_WAIT`; they are cited by `cpp:Executor::spin_once` and `cpp:Client::wait_for_service`.
